citation: Chen H, Qiu M, Xu H, Guo P, Peng Y. Application of Metagenomics Next-Generation Sequencing on Diagnosis of Disseminated Infection Caused by Rhizomucor pusillus. Infection and Drug Resistance. 2024;17:5707-5713.
study_period: Not applicable (single case; pediatric ALL patient, First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou)

population.population_description: 4-year-old male with newly diagnosed ALL (day 18 fever during chemotherapy) with disseminated Rhizomucor pusillus infection
population.haemato_subtypes: B-ALL (naive B cells ~41.4%; HLA-DR, CD34, CD10, CD19, CD20, CD22, CD79a, CD38+)

neutropenic_status: Neutropenia during chemotherapy implied; neutropenia counts in case text (0.40 x 10^9/L leukocytes reported at admission)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS of BALF (Table 1 lists reads/coverage/relative abundance); laboratory/vendor not specified in extracted text

reference_standard: Clinical plus radiology and treatment response; conventional culture in this case did not detect R. pusillus

diagnostic_yield.n_positive_relevant_pathogens: R. pusillus detected in BALF by mNGS

additional_yield_vs_conventional: Culture did not detect R. pusillus; mNGS enabled prompt diagnosis of disseminated mucormycosis.
therapy_change: Treatment timeline (Figure 3) with antifungal changes; details not extractable as counts
mortality_or_outcomes: Not extractable (outcome discussed in case narrative)
quadas2_notes: Case report, n=1. Per protocol rule 4, not usable for pooled analysis. No denominator, no 2x2.

evidence_quotes.quote: A 4-year-old male was admitted to the hospital (the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat sen University, Guangzhou, China) who was diagnosed with ALL for 1 week and returned to the hospital for chemotherapy.
mNGS facilitates prompt diagnosis of disseminated R. pusillus
